findings.description: The reach check only counts JS/TS-extension files as importers, so a .vue/.svelte/.astro/.mdx/index.html/package.json file that names a changed `*.test.ts` is dropped and the test stays in the test count.
findings.body:
**Non-JS importers never count as reaching a test file.**

```ts
const importer = entry.slice(prefix.length);
if (!isSourceFile(importer)) continue;
```

`isSourceFile` (`src/adapters/typescript-source.utils.ts`) accepts only `.ts .tsx .mts .cts .js .mjs .cjs .jsx`. `git grep -l` does list every other file that spells the test's name, but this line drops it before reading it. That includes files that load modules as production code:
- Vue/Svelte/Astro components: `<script lang="ts">import { api } from './big.test.js';</script>`
- a Vite `index.html` entry: `<script type="module" src="/src/main.test.ts">`
- `.mdx`, which decision 110 itself counts as source because it "compiles to a component"
- `package.json` `main`/`bin`/`exports` naming the emitted `dist/*.test.js`

The attack decision 110 closes still works through this route: 2000 lines of exports in `src/big.test.ts` plus one test behind `if (process.env.VITEST)`, imported from `src/App.vue`, read as "0 source + 2000 test". Pupitre gates any repo (docs/07-onboarding.md), so a Vue or Svelte app under the TypeScript adapter is a normal target. This is not one of decision 110's owed gaps: the specifier is static and spells the name, and the file is dropped only because of its extension.

Fix: widen the importer set to the non-JS module formats a bundler loads (`.vue`, `.svelte`, `.astro`, `.mdx`, `.html`, `package.json`), or scan every non-docs path that grep lists, which only over-counts (the safe direction). If the set stays as it is, list this in decision 110 as an owed gap.

findings.description: A relative specifier that resolves to any existing file stops the search with `continue`, so a decoy `src/big.test.js` next to `src/big.test.ts` makes the gate resolve `./big.test.js` to the decoy while tsc (NodeNext) compiles the real test file.
The reach check costs (tokens in an importer) × (changed targets), with no dedupe and no timeout on the synchronous loop, so a session can stall the shared merge lock and `pup review` for minutes.

The rename guard only covers source→test: lines landed as test (or docs) in one merge and later moved to source by `git mv` or a one-line `export * from './big.test.js'` never count as source in full.
findings.body:
**Lines can enter as test or docs, then become source without ever being counted as source.**

```ts
const isTest = (candidate: string): boolean => candidate.endsWith(DIFF_SIZE_TEST_SUFFIX);
if (isTest(path) && (entry?.renamedFrom === undefined || isTest(entry.renamedFrom))) {
  return 'test';
}
return 'source';
```

The guard fires only when the *new* path is a test name.

- **Merge 1** lands 2000 lines of production code plus one test in an unimported `src/big.test.ts`. They count as test and pass. Before this PR, this merge flagged.
- **Merge 2** runs `git mv src/big.test.ts src/big.ts`. Numstat pairs the rename, so `countChangedLines` (L433-439) adds only the edited delta to `counts.source`. The same works from `docs/x.md`.
- **Simpler merge 2:** add one line, `export * from './big.test.js'`. The reach check only looks at `*.test.ts` files changed in *this* diff (L433), so a test landed earlier is never checked.
- **Copy variant:** shared-config `diff.renames=copies` pairs a test→source copy in `gitDiffNumstat`, which does not pin rename detection.

Decision 110 closes the opposite direction (`git mv big.ts big.test.ts`) but does not list cross-merge accumulation as owed.

Fix, in two parts:
1. Count a file renamed or copied from a test/docs name onto a source name at full size, or pin `--no-renames` on the count's numstat.
2. Run the reach check on every `*.test.ts` on the branch that changed non-test code names, not just tests changed in this diff.

Otherwise, record this as an owed gap in decision 110.

findings.description: A symlink counts as 1 source line, but the docs file it points to keeps its docs classification: `src/pkg/impl.py -> ../../docs/impl.md` with 2000 lines of code reads as "1 source + 0 test + 2000 docs".

Docusaurus (v2/v3, default `markdown.format: 'mdx'`, content folder `docs/`) compiles `docs/*.md` as MDX, so JS/JSX in a `.md` file importable from `src/` counts as docs; decision 110's reason for counting `.mdx` as source applies to `.md` in those repos.
findings.body:
**In a Docusaurus repo, `.md` under `docs/` is code.**

```ts
export const DIFF_SIZE_DOCS_EXTENSIONS = ['.md', '.rst', '.adoc'];
```

Decision 110 names Docusaurus as a project that keeps running code under `docs/`, and counts `.mdx` as source because it "compiles to a component". Docusaurus v3 defaults `markdown.format` to `'mdx'` (v2 also ran `.md` through the MDX loader), and its docs plugin reads root `docs/` by default. So a `docs/*.md` file can export JS/JSX, and `src/` can import it via `@site/docs/x.md`.

In such a repo, 2000 lines of exported code in `docs/big.md`, imported from `src/`, read as "0 source + 2000 docs" and pass the flag. This is the same pattern the PR closed for `*.test.ts`. The owed list in decision 110 does not cover it. Knowledge of Docusaurus defaults is pinned, not read in-tree, hence medium confidence.

Fix options:
- count `docs/**/*.md` as source when the branch has a root `docusaurus.config.*`;
- run the reach check over changed docs paths too;
- at minimum, record this as an owed gap in decision 110.

findings.description: The review queue only uses `source + test + docs`, which the reach check never changes, yet `countChangedLines` now runs a raw diff, a full `ls-tree`, a tree-wide `git grep` and per-file `cat-file` for every queued session. Its new throw paths (grep exit ≠ 0/1, unexpected listing entry) can abort the whole review listing. Give the queue a plain total, or let the caller skip classification.

No review-queue test commits a `*.test.ts` or `docs/*.md` file, so changing `changedLines = source + test + docs` to `source` would pass every test, even though decision 110 says the queue keeps counting every changed line.

The test 'follows test files re-exporting one another to production code' changes all three chained tests on the branch, so they are all first-round targets and the multi-round `git grep` loop in `reachableTestFiles` never runs. Commit `a.test.ts` and `b.test.ts` on the base first so the test proves the chain is followed.

About 135 lines of TypeScript import-graph analysis (`testStem`, `tokensHolding`, `filesNaming`, `reachableTestFiles`) land in the 2,600-line gate service. They import a language-specific adapter util (`typescript-source.utils`) that no other `src/core/` module uses, and they caused the +44 complexity flag. Consider a dedicated module next to the TypeScript adapter.

`rawDiffEntries` is a branch-diff parser outside `git-diff.client.ts`, and it retypes the `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS` hardening flags inline. A flag later added to `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS` would silently miss this call.

`testStem` hardcodes `'.ts'.length` instead of deriving it from `DIFF_SIZE_TEST_SUFFIX`, and the test-suffix rule is spelled separately at L268, L275 and L389. If the constant widens, `testStem` cuts the wrong stem and `git grep` searches for the wrong names.

The new `git grep`, `ls-tree` and per-file `cat-file` calls run inside the merge lock without `timeout: GATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`, unlike the existing gate-time tree read in `git-tree.client.ts`, whose comment says every child pup runs is timed out.

The git symlink mode `'120000'` is an inline literal, against docs/conventions/general.md §No hardcoded values. The function's other tunables live in `merge-gate.constants.ts`. Add a named constant there.
Decision 110 is inserted between 105 and 106, so the file reads 105, 110, 106, 107 while decisions are otherwise in order. Move it to the end of the file.
The §No hardcoded values example still quotes the old `DIFF_SIZE_FLAG_LINES` JSDoc ('adds + deletes, lockfiles excluded'), which this PR rewrote. The example now misquotes the file it cites.

The risk-score description still says 'diff size vs task size'. Decision 110 says the code never had a task-size comparison and only fixed the phrase in docs/04. It should say changed lines, tests and docs included.
docs/04 says binary files are left out of the count, but a text file git was told to call binary is recounted and flagged (decision 53, restated in decision 110). Say 'genuinely binary files'.

A `.ts`/`.js` file with a NUL byte in a leading comment (first 8000 bytes) is a 'real binary' to git, so its lines count zero toward diff size, yet JS/TS still compiles and runs it. Unchanged by this PR; decision 53 doesn't consider source that tolerates a NUL.
